RFI: A request for information that asks the responsible person to resolve a missing or conflicting requirement.
actual: The physical dimension observed or specified for the identified material, rather than its size name.
area: The amount of two-dimensional surface or cross-section, expressed in square units.
as-built: A drawing that records the supported observed condition of an assembly.
brace: A member that constrains movement or transfers load through a frame.
bubble: A pocket of gas within the liquid in a level vial.
calibration: Establishing how an instrument's indications relate to reference values under stated conditions.
cause: A condition or change that produces an observed effect.
centerline: A reference line through the middle of a feature or member.
chain: A sequence of dimensions or measurements taken successively from the previous point.
clear gap: The unobstructed distance between the facing edges of two objects.
clearance: Space required between an object and a boundary or another object.
conflict: A situation in which two or more stated requirements cannot all be met as drawn.
connection: The joint or interface through which parts meet and interact.
constraint: A condition that a proposed solution must satisfy.
contact: Where the instrument or object touches the measured surface.
controlled test: A comparison that changes a selected factor while holding other relevant conditions consistent.
coordinate: Check related work together so dimensions, routes and requirements agree.
datum: A specified reference point, line or surface from which dimensions are taken.
depth: Distance through a space or object in the stated direction.
deviation: The measured value minus the specified target, including its positive or negative sign.
diagonal: A line joining nonadjacent corners of a shape.
diameter: A straight-line distance across a circle through its center.
discrepancy: A difference between records, requirements or observations that needs explanation.
elevation: Vertical position relative to a stated datum.
endpoint: The point where a measured length begins or ends.
envelope: The full outside space occupied or required by an object or route.
equivalent: Representing the same quantity or relationship in a different form.
estimate: An approximate value based on stated observations, assumptions or a model.
evidence: Observations or measurements used to support or challenge a conclusion.
fall: The decrease in elevation from upstream to downstream over the stated run.
finished surface: The final exposed surface used by a person, such as a tread or floor finish.
flow direction: The direction in which material is intended or observed to move.
front: The designated primary viewing direction in an orthographic drawing.
gauge: A size designation or measuring device; in this lesson AWG names a standardized wire-size series.
high point: The location at the greatest elevation within the stated comparison.
inside diameter: The diameter of the internal opening of a tube or pipe.
interval: The span between two specified values, marks or positions.
joint: The interface or material between adjoining units or members.
level: Horizontal, perpendicular to local vertical; also an instrument used to check that condition.
liquid: A material that flows and takes the shape of its container while retaining approximately its volume.
lower limit: The smallest permitted value in a stated interval.
measurement: A value obtained by comparing a quantity with a defined unit or reference.
model: A simplified representation used to explain or predict a specified situation.
module: A repeating coordination dimension, such as a masonry unit plus its specified joint.
nominal: A standardized size name that may differ from a directly measured dimension.
offset: A positional difference or a difference between an indicated value and a reference.
outside diameter: The diameter across the exterior of a round tube or pipe.
percent: A ratio expressed per hundred after quantities are put in compatible units.
plan: A drawing viewed from above that locates features horizontally.
prediction: A stated expected result made before the relevant check or observation.
racking: A change of frame angles that distorts an intended rectangular shape.
ratio: One quantity compared by division with another, with units made explicit.
rectangle: A four-sided figure with four right angles.
reference: A known value, point or object used for comparison.
repeat: Carry out the measurement or trial again under stated conditions.
resolution: The smallest change an instrument can distinguish or display.
reversal: Turning an instrument to a specified opposite orientation to compare its readings.
revise: Change an earlier artifact or conclusion in response to identified evidence or feedback.
revision: An identified version of a document with its changes recorded.
right view: An orthographic view from the designated right side of an object.
rise: The vertical increase or distance between stated elevations.
riser: The vertical height between successive stair walking surfaces; also the vertical face at that step.
run: The horizontal distance used in the stated slope calculation.
scale: The ratio of a drawing dimension to the corresponding real dimension.
section: A view that shows a specified cut through an object or assembly.
sensitivity: How much an instrument indication changes for a given change in the measured quantity.
settle: Reach a sufficiently stationary state for the intended reading.
slope: Vertical change divided by horizontal run, with units or ratio convention stated.
spacing: The distance between repeated specified reference points, such as member centers.
specification: The stated required dimensions, conditions or performance for a task.
spread: The highest reading minus the lowest reading in the set being compared.
square: At right angles in the intended layout; also a tool used to check right angles.
support: A member or contact that carries or restrains another part of an assembly.
systematic: Describes an effect that consistently biases measurements under the stated conditions.
thickness: The distance between opposing surfaces of a layer or part.
tolerance: The permitted variation from a specified value.
top: The orthographic view looking down on the designated object.
transport: Movement of material from one location to another.
triangle: A shape with three sides and three angles.
upper limit: The largest permitted value in a stated interval.
vertical: The local up-down direction aligned with gravity.
wall thickness: The distance through the material forming a tube or pipe wall.
